::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Part IV · Translating models into practice** · **Level:** independent application · **Teaching units:** 29–32
(4 × 45 min) · **Required reading:** core readings of B27 and B28 (about 20 minutes) ·
**Project material:** [colloquium, feedback and evaluation](../exercises/project-colloquium.qmd)
:::

## Guiding question

**Which recommendation can we defend today, under which conditions, against which counter-position, and what will
we check next?**

## Learning objectives

By the end of this workshop you can

1. defend a model and a recommendation in ten minutes and answer critical questions in four;
2. take a critical perspective (clinic, patients, regulation, data protection, security, methods) on another
   group's project and formulate a concrete change request;
3. compare the consequences of a wrong decision across clinic, laboratory and care system and state an override or
   stop condition;
4. revise your recommendation after peer review and document what changed and why;
5. transfer the approach to a new research or care problem of your own choice.

## Preparation

- **Required reading** (about 20 minutes):
  [B27 · Model passport, study report and decision – core reading](https://cttir.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b27-model-passport-study-report.html#sec-b27-core)
  and
  [B28 · Case atlas, glossary and transfer – core reading](https://cttir.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b28-case-atlas-glossary.html#sec-b28-core).
- **Submit before W8** (deadline set by the course team): decision sheet (one page), model passport (one page) and
  the commented R script with its start command. See the [project brief](../exercises/project-brief.qmd).
- **Prepare** a ten-minute presentation following the [colloquium format](../exercises/project-colloquium.qmd).

## Teaching units

| Unit | Task | Minutes | Observable evidence |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 29 | Groups 1–3 each defend their model for ten minutes and answer questions for four minutes. The other groups each represent one critical perspective. | 45 | Three assessable presentations and one recorded change request each. |
| 30 | Groups 4–6 present in the same format. Everyone compares the consequences of a wrong decision across clinic, laboratory and care system. | 45 | A criteria-based comparison and a reasoned override or stop condition. |
| 31 | Individual examination with 20 case-based single-best-answer questions in 25 minutes, including briefing, distribution and collection. | 45 | Individual examination performance. The public course offers specially developed practice cases instead ([self-test](../exercises/self-test.qmd)). |
| 32 | A peer checks each revised recommendation and its evidence. Anonymous evaluation, review of W1 and choice of a next research or care problem. | 45 | A revision note and an individual transfer task. |

### Time plan for units 29 and 30

Three groups fit into 45 minutes: 3 × (10 minutes presentation + 4 minutes questions) = 42 minutes, plus
3 minutes for changing over. The course team keeps time strictly; the questions are asked by the groups holding
the critical perspectives, in an order drawn at the start.

### About the examination (unit 31)

The examination covers all four parts with the distribution shown in the [syllabus](../syllabus.qmd#assessment).
Questions are new cases; none of them is published. The [formative self-test](../exercises/self-test.qmd) shows
the type of reasoning expected, with explained answers. Assessment and participation conditions for a particular
run of the course are announced by the course team before the course starts.

### Review and short case B (unit 32)

Rate the four statements from the [entry self-assessment in W1](w1-from-clinical-case-to-question.qmd#self-assessment)
again, anonymously. Then work on **short case B** for five minutes, on paper and without help:

> A clinical team reports "0.91 AUC on 3,000 video frames" for a model that detects an abnormal gait pattern in
> videos from 15 patients. Frames from every patient were used both for training and for testing. A week later a
> colleague notices that a screenshot from one of the videos, showing a patient's face and the ward's name board,
> was posted in a group chat that includes an external collaborator.
>
> (a) What is the independent number of units in the test? (b) What does the 0.91 measure? (c) Name the first two
> steps after the screenshot is discovered.

The course team compares the anonymous answers to short cases A and B. The comparison is used to revise the
course; it is not a measure of individual performance, and a difference between before and after is not proof
that the course caused it.

## Materials

- [Colloquium, feedback and evaluation](../exercises/project-colloquium.qmd): presentation brief, feedback
  cards, change request, transfer question and the anonymous evaluation form.
- [Project rubric](../exercises/project-rubric.qmd) with the scoring rule.

## Four perspectives in this workshop

The critical perspectives in units 29 and 30 are assigned so that every project is questioned on ethics,
regulation, data protection and security, plus clinical use and methods. Each question is recorded with the answer
and, where needed, a change request.

## After the course

The transfer task from unit 32 is yours. The [case atlas in B28](https://cttir.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b28-case-atlas-glossary.html)
helps you find the method that fits a new problem, starting from the decision rather than from the data type.
